annotations.title: Generate calendar event file and links

description: Use this when the user wants a calendar invite, an .ics file, or an add-to-calendar link (Google Calendar, Outlook, Office 365, Yahoo) for one event or one repeating event: a webinar, class, meeting, party, deadline, or launch. Takes the title, local start/end and the event's time zone (city or IANA zone), or dates only for all-day events, plus optional location, description, link, organizer name, reminders, and a repeat rule (daily, weekly on chosen weekdays, monthly by date, nth weekday such as the last Friday, or the first/last weekday of the month, yearly; with count, until date, and skipped dates). Returns a downloadable RFC 5545 .ics file with time zone data, four add-to-calendar links, and the first 5 dates in the event's zone and optional attendee zones, with daylight saving changes flagged. Does not send invitations, read or change anyone's calendar, or track RSVPs. Do not use for a list of different sessions (use generate_event_series) or for finding a meeting time across zones.

all_day.description: true for an all-day event (dates only), e.g. a conference day or a deadline. Automatic when start has no time.

description.description: Event details or agenda (plain text; line breaks allowed), e.g. Bring a laptop.

duration_minutes.description: Length in minutes instead of end, e.g. 90.

end.description: Local end YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM, or just a time HH:MM on the start day, e.g. 21:00. For all-day events, the last day YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive). Default: 1 hour, or 1 day for all-day.

location.description: Venue, address, or meeting room shown in the calendar, e.g. Pier 39, San Francisco.

organizer_name.description: Optional organizer name shown in the details, e.g. Acme Events. No email needed.

count.description: Total number of dates in the pattern, e.g. 10. Do not combine with until.

exceptions.description: Dates YYYY-MM-DD to skip, e.g. ["2026-12-24"]. Each must be a date the pattern produces.

frequency.description: How often it repeats, e.g. weekly.

interval.description: Repeat every N days/weeks/months/years, e.g. 2 for every other week. Default 1.

monthly_on.description: Monthly/yearly: day_of_month (same date, e.g. the 15th; default) or nth_weekday (e.g. the second Tuesday or the last Friday).

nth.description: With nth_weekday: 1-5, or -1 for the last, e.g. 2 for the second Tuesday. Default: the start date's position in its month.

until.description: Last possible date YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive), e.g. 2027-06-30. Leave out count and until for no end date.

weekdays.description: Weekly: the days it repeats on, e.g. ["TU","TH"] (default: the start's weekday). Monthly/yearly with nth_weekday: one weekday, e.g. ["TU"], or several with nth to pick from the set, e.g. ["MO","TU","WE","TH","FR"] with nth -1 for the last weekday of the month.

reminders_minutes_before.description: Up to 3 reminders in minutes before the start, e.g. [15, 1440] for 15 minutes and 1 day before.

start.description: Local start YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM in the event's time zone, e.g. 2026-11-05T18:30, or a date YYYY-MM-DD for an all-day event. No UTC offset.

time_zone.description: Time zone of the start/end: IANA zone (Europe/Warsaw), city (Chicago, Sydney), or UTC. Required for timed events; not used for all-day events.

title.description: Event title, e.g. Product launch webinar.

url.description: Optional event page or video-call link, e.g. https://example.com/webinar.

viewer_time_zones.description: Optional places or zones of attendees to show local times for, e.g. ["New York", "Tokyo"].

name: generate_calendar_event
title: Generate calendar event file and links
